Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.question_text: (a) Using the substitution $$u=2^{x}$$, show that the equation $$4^{x}-2^{x+1}-15=0$$ can be written in the form $$u^{2}-2u-15=0$$. (b) Hence solve $$4^{x}-2^{x+1}-15=0$$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.hint: Use $$4^{x}=(2^{2})^{x}=2^{2x}$$ and $$2^{x+1}=2\cdot2^{x}$$; then solve the quadratic in $$u$$ and back-substitute $$u=2^{x}$$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$(a)\ 4^{x}-2^{x+1}-15=0\Rightarrow(2^{2})^{x}-2\cdot2^{x}-15=0\Rightarrow2^{2x}-2\cdot2^{x}-15=0.$$ With $$u=2^{x}$$ this becomes $$u^{2}-2u-15=0.$$ $$(b)\ u^{2}-2u-15=0\Rightarrow(u-5)(u+3)=0\Rightarrow u=5\ (\text{since }u>0).$$ Thus $$2^{x}=5\Rightarrow x=\log_{2}5=\dfrac{\ln5}{\ln2}\approx2.32\ \text{(2 d.p.)}.$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.question_text: Solve the following equations, giving exact solutions: (a) $$\ln(2x-5)=8$$ (b) $$e^{4x}=5$$ (c) $$24-e^{-2x}=10$$ (d) $$\ln x+\ln(x-3)=0$$ (e) $$e^{x}+e^{-x}=2$$ (f) $$\ln2+\ln x=4$$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.hint: Rewrite logs/exponentials, isolate $$x$$ using $$e^{\ln y}=y$$ and standard algebra; for (e) set $$u=e^{x}$$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$(a)\ \ln(2x-5)=8\Rightarrow2x-5=e^{8}\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{e^{8}+5}{2}.$$ $$(b)\ e^{4x}=5\Rightarrow4x=\ln5\Rightarrow x=\tfrac14\ln5.$$ $$(c)\ 24-e^{-2x}=10\Rightarrow e^{-2x}=14\Rightarrow-2x=\ln14\Rightarrow x=-\tfrac12\ln14.$$ $$(d)\ \ln x+\ln(x-3)=\ln[x(x-3)]=0\Rightarrow x(x-3)=1\Rightarrow x^{2}-3x-1=0,$$ $$x=\dfrac{3\pm\sqrt{13}}{2},\ \text{but domain }x>3\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3+\sqrt{13}}{2}.$$ $$(e)\ e^{x}+e^{-x}=2;\ \text{let }u=e^{x}\Rightarrow u+\dfrac1u=2\Rightarrow u^{2}-2u+1=0\Rightarrow(u-1)^{2}=0\Rightarrow u=1,$$ $$e^{x}=1\Rightarrow x=0.$$ $$(f)\ \ln2+\ln x=\ln(2x)=4\Rightarrow2x=e^{4}\Rightarrow x=\tfrac12e^{4}.$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.question_text: Solve for $a$ given that the equation $$e^{x}=ax+1$$ has a repeated root.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.hint: Use tangency: at a repeated root $x=r$, both $f(r)=0$ and $f'(r)=0$ for $f(x)=e^x-ax-1$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}\text{Let }f(x)&=e^x-ax-1\\\text{Repeated root at }x=r&\Rightarrow f(r)=0,\ f'(r)=0\\f'(x)&=e^x-a\\f'(r)=0&\Rightarrow e^r=a\\f(r)=0&\Rightarrow e^r-ar-1=0\\\text{Sub }a=e^r:\ e^r-e^r r-1&=0\\e^r(1-r)&=1\\e^r&=\frac{1}{1-r}\\\text{But }a=e^r&\Rightarrow a=\frac{1}{1-r}\\\text{Also }e^r=\frac{1}{1-r}&\Rightarrow (1-r)e^r=1\\\text{Solve: try }r=0\Rightarrow (1)e^0=1&\checkmark\\\therefore r=0,\ a=e^0=1\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.hint: Start with the domain $x>2$, combine logs, then solve the resulting rational inequality carefully.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}\ln x+\ln(x-2)&\ge \ln(3x)\\\text{Domain: }x>0,\ x-2>0&\Rightarrow x>2\\\ln(x(x-2))&\ge \ln(3x)\\\text{Since }\ln \text{ is increasing: }x(x-2)&\ge 3x\\x^2-2x-3x&\ge 0\\x^2-5x&\ge 0\\x(x-5)&\ge 0\\\text{With }x>2,\ x>0&\Rightarrow x-5\ge0\\\therefore\ x&\ge 5\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}P(2)=5P_0&\Rightarrow 5P_0=P_0e^{2k}\Rightarrow e^{2k}=5\Rightarrow k=\frac12\ln5\\P(6)=125P_0&\Rightarrow 125=P_0e^{6k}/P_0=e^{6k}\\\text{Using }k=\frac12\ln5:\ e^{6k}&=e^{3\ln5}=5^3=125\ \checkmark\\\therefore\ k&=\frac12\ln5\ \text{and model is consistent.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.question_text: Show that $$f(x)=\ln x-\frac{1}{x}$$ is increasing for $x>0$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.hint: Compute $f'(x)$ and show it is positive for all $x>0$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=\ln x-\frac{1}{x}\\f'(x)&=\frac1x+\frac{1}{x^2}=\frac{x+1}{x^2}\\\text{For }x>0:\ x^2>0\ \text{and }x+1>0&\Rightarrow f'(x)>0\\\therefore\ f(x)&\text{ is increasing on }(0,\infty)\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.question_text: Solve $$e^{x}=\frac{1}{1-x}$$ for real $x$ and state how many solutions exist.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.hint: Rearrange to $(1-x)e^x=1$ and analyze using monotonicity/derivatives; try $x=0$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}e^x&=\frac{1}{1-x}\ \Rightarrow\ (1-x)e^x=1\\\text{Check }x=0:\ (1-0)e^0&=1\Rightarrow 1=1\ \checkmark\\g(x)&=(1-x)e^x\\g'(x)&=-e^x+(1-x)e^x=(-1+1-x)e^x=-xe^x\\g'(x)&=0\text{ only at }x=0\\\text{For }x<0:\ g'(x)>0;\ \text{for }x>0:\ g'(x)<0&\Rightarrow x=0\text{ is a maximum}\\g(0)=1,\ \lim_{x\to1^-}g(x)=0,\ \lim_{x\to-\infty}g(x)=0&\Rightarrow g(x)\le1 \text{ with equality only at }0\\\therefore\ \text{Exactly one solution: }x&=0\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.question_text: Find the range of $$f(x)=e^x+e^{-x}$$ for real $x$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.hint: Use AM–GM or rewrite as $2\cosh x$; minimum occurs at $x=0$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=e^x+e^{-x}\\\text{By AM–GM: }e^x+e^{-x}&\ge2\sqrt{e^x\cdot e^{-x}}=2\\\text{Equality when }e^x=e^{-x}\Rightarrow x=0\\\therefore\ \min f&=2,\ \text{and }f(x)\to\infty\text{ as }|x|\to\infty\\\Rightarrow \text{Range }&=[2,\infty)\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.hint: Take $\ln$ both sides: $\ln y=x\ln x$, then differentiate implicitly.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}y&=x^x,\ x>0\\\ln y&=x\ln x\\\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{d}{dx}(x\ln x)=\ln x+1\\\frac{dy}{dx}&=y(\ln x+1)=x^x(\ln x+1)\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.question_text: Solve $$e^{x}\le x^2+2$$ for all real $x$ (show solution set).
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.hint: Consider $h(x)=x^2+2-e^x$, analyze turning points and sign changes (exact roots may be non-elementary; show interval form).
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}\text{Let }h(x)&=x^2+2-e^x\\h'(x)&=2x-e^x\\h''(x)&=2-e^x\\\text{Key values: }h(0)=2-1&=1>0,\ h(2)=6-e^2<0\\\text{So there is a root }r\in(0,2).\\\text{Also }h(-2)=6-e^{-2}>0&,\ \text{and as }x\to-\infty,\ h(x)\to\infty\\\text{Since }e^x\text{ eventually dominates }x^2,&\ \text{there is exactly one positive root }r\approx1.146\\\text{Thus }h(x)\ge0 \text{ for }x\le r&\ \Rightarrow e^x\le x^2+2\text{ for }x\le r\\\therefore\ \text{Solution set }&=(-\infty,r]\ \text{where }r\approx1.146\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.question_text: Find all real $a$ such that $$\ln(x+a)$$ is defined for all $x\ge0$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}\ln(x+a)\text{ defined }\forall x\ge0&\iff x+a>0\ \forall x\ge0\\\text{Minimum of }x\text{ on }[0,\infty)&\text{ is }0\\\therefore\ 0+a>0&\Rightarrow a>0\end{aligned}$$

Convert each side to natural logs then solve algebraically.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}\log_x16&=\log_2x\\\frac{\ln16}{\ln x}&=\frac{\ln x}{\ln2}\\(\ln x)^2&=\ln16\ln2\\\ln16=4\ln2\Rightarrow(\ln x)^2&=4(\ln2)^2\\\ln x&=\pm2\ln2\\x&=e^{2\ln2}=4\ \text{or}\ x=e^{-2\ln2}=\frac14\\\text{Base condition: }x>0,\ x\ne1&\Rightarrow \text{both valid}\\\therefore\ x&=4,\ \frac14\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.question_text: Find $a$ such that the curve $$y=\ln x$$ has a tangent at $x=a$ passing through the origin.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.hint: Equation of tangent: $y-\ln a=\frac1a(x-a)$. Set $(0,0)$ on line to solve for $a$.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}y&=\ln x\\\text{At }x=a:\ m&=\frac1a,\ \text{point }(a,\ln a)\\\text{Tangent: }y-\ln a&=\frac1a(x-a)\\\text{Passes through }(0,0):\ 0-\ln a&=\frac1a(0-a)=-1\\\ln a&=1\\a&=e\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.question_text: Determine the number of real solutions of $$e^x=x+3$$ and justify.
Chapter 14-Exponentials and log.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=e^x-x-3\\f'(x)&=e^x-1\\f'(x)=0&\Rightarrow x=0\\f''(x)&=e^x>0\Rightarrow \text{minimum at }x=0\\f(0)&=1-0-3=-2<0\\\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)&=\infty,\ \lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)=\infty\ (\text{since }-x\to\infty)\\\text{With a single minimum below 0, }f(x)=0&\text{ has exactly two real roots.}\end{aligned}$$
